review_notes: I read the whole file and the HeadTransport, HeadCut and solution sections in detail. I did not open the imported theorem files, so I did not check whether the repeated pieces already exist in them. I only grepped for the pullback-square pattern inside the target file. I found three repeated blocks: a near-verbatim copy of a lemma's proof (finding 1), a pullback-square paste repeated five times (finding 2), and the H0/H1 baseChange pair (finding 3). Nothing here was compiled. The proposed rewrites assume variable and instance contexts as described, and they may need small adjustments. In particular, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_snd_of_smooth` has to be moved or re-stated before `range_fst_subset_of_smooth_of_hUmax`. `range_fst_subset_of_smooth_of_hUmax` appears unused in `solution`.

findings.problem: Lines 604–623 repeat the proof of `smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_snd_of_smooth` (lines 731–747) almost line for line. Both obtain geometric irreducibility from `geometricallyIrreducible_snd_of_smooth_of_hH0`. Both derive `IrreducibleSpace` from it and build `V := fst ⁻¹ᵁ U`. Both prove `V` nonempty through `sectionFibrePoint ε`, and both paste the restricted pullback square. Both finish with `smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_irreducibleSpace`. The only differences are the names `x` and `s`, and the extra `IsProper` instance that `range_fst_subset_of_smooth_of_hUmax` carries. The nonemptiness argument and the square paste are real mathematical content, and a fix to one copy has to be made in the other too.

Keep `[IsNoetherianRing R] [Flat c] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation c]` as its hypotheses. Its proof does not appear to use `IsProper`. findings.problem: The same pullback-pasting argument appears five times with different instantiations. Take `isPullback_morphismRestrict` for `fst ∣_ U`, then `paste_vert` with `IsPullback.of_hasPullback`, giving the square `(fst ∣_ U) / ((fst ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ snd) / (U.ι ≫ f) / g`. The occurrences are at lines 160–165, 313–316, 618–620, 708–711 and 743–745. The long `have hsq … have hbig …` statements are rewritten each time. Two of them (158–166 and 617–621) then apply `smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback`. Line 711 applies the same base-change step for `Smooth`, and 313–316 applies it for `IsAffineHom`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in `HeadTransport`, stated for `{X S T : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ S) (U : X.Opens)`: `IsPullback ((pullback.fst f g) ∣_ U) ((pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) (U.ι ≫ f) g`. Its proof is `(isPullback_morphismRestrict _ _).paste_vert (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f g)`. Add a corollary `smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_restrict_pullback`: from `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (U.ι ≫ f)` it gives `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((pullback.fst f g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ pullback.snd f g)`, via `of_isPullback`. Then `smooth_U_baseChange` is the corollary at `f := c`, `g := specMap R A` (with `baseChange R c A` unfolded to `pullback.snd c (specMap R A)`). The two smoothness blocks at 617–621 and 743–746 become the same one-line call. `hcov_baseChange` and `smooth_snd_of_not_mem_badLocus` use the square lemma directly with their own `MorphismProperty.of_isPullback` or `IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback` step.
findings.benefit: The five hand-written `hsq/hbig` pairs (plus the smoothness step in three of them) collapse to one square lemma and one corollary. The call sites show their real content: smoothness of the restriction in two places, affineness of `g` in `hcov_baseChange`, and smoothness over the smooth locus in `smooth_snd_of_not_mem_badLocus`. Stating the square once also removes the risk of the copies drifting apart.

findings.problem: `hg_baseChange` (H1) and `h0_baseChange` (H0) have the same proof. Both introduce `k`, `x'` and `𝒲`, and obtain `φ` from `exists_cutFibreIso_baseChange`. Both call `exists_linearEquiv_sectionsOf_of_iso` with the same long argument list, including `(Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorUnitObjIso φ.hom).symm`. Both then `change` to the `𝟙_` form, rewrite with `finrank_eq`, and apply the hypothesis at `x' ≫ specMap R A`. They differ only in which component of the obtained 5-tuple is kept (`e1` versus `e0`). The statements also repeat the long fibre-module expressions.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma `exists_cover_equiv_baseChange` stating: for `x'` and `𝒲` as in these theorems, `∃ 𝒱 : (pullback (pullback.snd c (𝟙 _)) (x' ≫ specMap R A)).TwoAffineOpenCover, Nonempty (H0 of 𝒲-sections of the base-changed unit ≃ₗ[k] H0 of 𝒱-sections of the unit on c) ∧ Nonempty (the same for H1)`. Its proof is the `obtain` at lines 120–124 followed by the `change` that turns the unit sheaf into `𝟙_ _`. Both `hg_baseChange` and `h0_baseChange` then destructure its output, rewrite with `e.finrank_eq`, and apply `hg` or `h0`. This is a moderate gain, since the duplication is a pair of 20-line proofs, not a deep argument.
findings.benefit: The transport of the cover and of the H0/H1 equivalences is written and checked once. A change to the cover-transport call, for example if the signature of `exists_linearEquiv_sectionsOf_of_iso` changes, is made in a single place.
